sketches.title: Viewing Withheld
sketches.premise: You are estate agents listing a terrible room. Each round, the card gives one bleak feature and one ordinary object; write a property listing that makes the feature sound like a luxury without pretending it is gone. The host awards points for the most heroic spin that leaves the bad truth standing.
sketches.criterion: The listing must keep the card's terrible feature true while making the named object part of the sales pitch.
sketches.move_shape: Write one listing line under 90 characters, not a question or comment. Example: card: 'No window / chair' → 'Chair enjoys our exclusive permanent night retreat.'

sketches.title: Floor Plan Fiction
sketches.premise: A card gives two dull facts about a dreadful room. Turn them into a tiny floor-plan note: place the two named things together and give their arrangement an absurd but possible purpose. The host checks the room still has both things in the stated places, then rewards the strangest useful explanation.
sketches.criterion: Your note must preserve both given objects and their stated positions while inventing what the arrangement is for.
sketches.move_shape: Write one floor-plan annotation under 90 characters. Example: card: 'Bed by door / sink under stairs' → 'Emergency bunk beside the exit; wash station below.'
sketches.first_card: Toilet by the desk / radiator behind the bed

sketches.title: Agent After Dark
sketches.premise: The card states a real, unexciting fact about a bad room and names two objects in it. Write the agent's spoken line to a doubtful buyer, keeping the fact audible but wrapping it in a suspicious little story. Points go to the furthest tale that still leaves the room honestly terrible.
sketches.criterion: The spoken line must retain the card's fact and use both named objects without contradicting either.
sketches.move_shape: Write one line of dialogue under 90 characters, with no question to the host. Example: card: 'The room is cold / mirror and lamp' → 'The lamp stays lit; the mirror confirms the frost is real.'
sketches.first_card: The carpet is wet / sofa and bucket

sketches.title: Amenity or Warning
sketches.premise: Each card offers a bad room feature and two objects. Label the feature as a named amenity, then explain how the objects support that label. The joke is to make a warning sound like a brochure feature while keeping the warning completely checkable.
sketches.criterion: Your amenity must still mean the card's bad feature is true and must give both objects a role.
sketches.move_shape: Write an amenity name plus one explanation under 90 characters. Example: card: 'No lock / bell and coat hook' → 'Security-free entry: bell for drama, hook for the getaway coat.'
sketches.first_card: The room smells of paint / fan and curtains

sketches.title: Inventory of Regret
sketches.premise: You receive two objects from a terrible room and one plain fact about them. Write an inventory entry that gives the pair a shared history, warning or purpose. Keep the fact intact; the host rewards the most elaborate past that the objects can survive.
sketches.criterion: The entry must keep the card's fact about both objects true and connect the objects in one invented explanation.
sketches.move_shape: Write one labelled inventory entry under 90 characters. Example: card: 'Two chairs are broken / bell and tray' → 'Breakfast set, damaged in a polite escape attempt.'
sketches.first_card: The bed has one leg missing / alarm clock and suitcase

sketches.title: Small-Print Palace
sketches.premise: The card gives a true drawback of a terrible room and two things found there. Write the tiny legal note beneath its listing: technically honest, wildly unhelpful, and keen to make the drawback sound intentional. The host scores how far the wording travels without hiding the truth.
sketches.criterion: The small print must state or clearly preserve the drawback and mention both named things as part of its explanation.
sketches.move_shape: Write one legal-style note under 90 characters. Example: card: 'The door sticks / key and doormat' → 'Key supplied; doormat included for those awaiting entry.'
sketches.first_card: The shower has no hot water / towel and mug
